newsitem.title: USA: Chancellor bondholders cheer Evergreen merger.
newsitem.headline: Chancellor bondholders cheer Evergreen merger.

text.p: Owners of Chancellor Broadcasting Co bonds and preferred stock reacted positively to the news on Tuesday that Evergreen Media Corp had agreed to buy the company as well at 10 radio properties owned by Viacom Inc.

Chancellor's $300 million in exchangeable PIK preferred stock rose around three points to 103 1/2 in trading on Tuesday, traders said. The company's 9 3/8 percent bonds rose 1 1/2 to two points to 102 bid, traders said.

"The move is a reflection of the fact that the company has a more diverse asset based and a broader persence in several important markets such as New York and Los Angeles," said Steven Shapiro, high-yield broadcasting analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp.
But Shapiro added, "This event is only a slight credit positive for bondholders. The new entity will be fairly leveraged with debt-to-cash flow north of six times for 1997."
In a conference call with analysts on Tuesday, company executives said Chancellor will pay $1.075 billion for Viacom's radio properties.
The executives said they planned to finance the acquisition by obtaining $615 million in bank loans and issuing $200 million in junk bonds and $100 million in redemable PIK preferred stock.
An additional $235 million will be obtained by selling radio stations in areas which the company would exceed Federal Communications Commission's ownership limits, they said.
Evergreen will finance its purchase of Chancellor through a stock swap and the assumption of around $900 million in Chancellor bonds and preferred stock, the executives said.

Shapiro said it is unlikely that the company will redeem Chancellor's debt in the near future given that the company is already borrowing a significant amount to finance the purchase of the Viacom assets.
He said redeeming Chancellor debt would also be an expensive proposition for Evergreen as the bonds and preferred stock have prepayment penalties and would have to be redeemed at a premium price.
An Evergreen spokesman said information about the issue was not immediately available.
